title: Add canary rollout tooling for tiered batching defaults (model/region percentage) + auto-rollback hooks
author: Benji Okafor
description: Motivation: We need a safe, repeatable mechanism to ramp tiered batching defaults by model+region (Hosted/Dedicated control plane) while protecting tail latency and error rates. This PR introduces a percentage-based canary rollout primitive (scoped to {model_family, model_variant, region}) and wires in automated rollback hooks that can be driven by SRE-defined signals (p95 latency, timeouts/cancels, queue delay, overload shed). Summary of changes: (1) New rollout spec + storage in control-plane config (validated, versioned, with dry-run validation) for `tiered_batching_defaults`. (2) Deterministic sampling: requests are assigned to canary/control based on stable hash of (route_id, customer_id, model_id, region) so we don’t thrash between buckets across retries. (3) Runtime/config service now returns both `batching_tier_default` and `rollout_bucket` metadata to support debugging and dashboards. (4) Auto-rollback: added a small rollback controller that listens to configured alert events (from existing alert webhook pipeline) and, when threshold is breached for a canary scope, automatically sets rollout percentage to 0 and posts an on-call note with the rollback reason + last-known metrics snapshot. (5) Guardrails: hard caps on max percentage change per hour, and a required “two-step” enablement for >25% (must be explicitly acknowledged via `rollout ack` command). Operational notes: The canary tooling is feature-flagged behind `tiered_batching_rollouts` and defaults OFF. No behavior changes unless rollout specs exist. Follow-ups: audit log enrichment is tracked separately; this PR uses existing config change auditing but does not yet add per-scope diff summaries.
commits: rollouts: deterministic sampler for model/region scoped ramp (stable hash bucketing)
config-service: expose effective tier defaults + rollout bucket metadata
rollback-controller: implement alert-driven rollback action + Slack/oncall payload
tests: unit coverage for sampler, validation, and rollback state transitions
docs: internal runbook snippet for enabling canaries and interpreting rollback reasons
notable_snippet: Example rollout spec (YAML): apiVersion: redwood.ai/v1 kind: TieredBatchingDefaultsRollout metadata: name: tbatch-defaults-ramp spec: scope: model_family: llama3 model_variant: llama3-70b region: us-west-2 route_id: chat.completions percentage: 5 seed: 20250306 guardrails: max_step_per_hour: 10 require_ack_over_percent: 25 rollback: enabled: true signals: - name: p95_latency_ms threshold: 1800 window: 10m - name: timeout_rate threshold: 0.02 window: 10m
review_conversation: Rafael Mendes: The auto-rollback needs to be conservative. If alerts flap, we’ll bounce configs. Can we add a minimum cooldown after rollback and require 2 consecutive windows before rollback triggers?

Benji Okafor (author): Added `rollback.cooldown_minutes` default 60 and changed trigger policy to require 2 consecutive windows above threshold. Also updated Slack payload to include both windows’ aggregates.
Allison Grant: Can we emit a metric for rollback actions and label it with scope keys? We’ll want dashboards/alerts on ‘rollbacks per day’ during beta.
Benji Okafor (author): Added `rollout_rollback_total{rollout_type,model_family,model_variant,region,route_id,reason}` + `rollout_rollback_last_timestamp` gauge. Hooked into existing metrics registry.
Ethan Park: Deterministic sampling key includes customer_id; what about anonymous traffic (no customer_id) and internal services? We need consistent bucketing across those too.

Benji Okafor (author): For missing customer_id we fall back to (api_key_id || org_id || request_origin) from auth context; if all missing, we use request_id which is stable per retry chain (propagated header). Added tests for each branch.
Marissa Cole: For >25% ramp requiring ack, can we make the CLI output a link to the runbook + remind operators about dashboards to watch?
Benji Okafor (author): CLI now prints runbook path + suggested dashboards (tiered latency, queue delay, timeout/cancel) and requires `--reason` string for audit trail.
Sergio Costa: Please ensure rollout bucket is present in tracing spans so we can filter traces by canary/control.
Benji Okafor (author): Added span attribute `rollout.bucket` and `rollout.scope_hash` in config resolution span; verified it shows up in staging traces.
rollout_notes: Staging validation: enabled 5% canary for llama3-70b in us-west-2 (chat.completions) with rollback enabled; verified bucket stability across retries and config explain endpoint shows `rollout_bucket=canary`; simulated alert webhook -> rollback set percentage to 0 and posted Slack notification; confirmed metrics emitted. Production: keep feature flag OFF until runtime-1.21 beta ramp; SRE to own alert wiring + thresholds per tier doc.
merge_summary: Merged to main after 2 review rounds. No API surface changes for customers. Canary rollout functionality is gated behind `tiered_batching_rollouts` and requires explicit rollout spec creation.
release_notes: Internal-only: Added rollout tooling to enable tiered batching defaults by model/region percentage with automatic rollback hooks and new rollback metrics. No customer-visible behavior unless enabled by operators.
